condition: Folder first with native Mac picker; Copy and Send together; separate Play step; optional tool chooser and Pause and Resume at workbook end.
scope: Ten synthetic personas × three independent HTML reads for each version. Each used the same question, model and OS assignments. Readers assumed access to Cowork and the demonstrations described in captions.
question:
Claude Desktop is already installed and your account has Cowork access. No course folder or previous course conversation exists. There is no trainer. You are trying this on your own.

Below is actual HTML from the handbook: navigation, cover, Start, contents and Prework, in their actual order. Cowork is selected; other runtime content is hidden and omitted. Initially closed panels show only their labels; their contents are available when opened. The Mac/Windows control starts on your computer's OS and can switch the setup directions. The rest of the handbook, including linked reading destinations, exists beyond this excerpt. Assess the start, not omitted later material. This is an HTML-reading simulation, not actual app execution or a visual screenshot test.

Based only on the HTML, describe what you would do, in order, until you could open and try the first game. Would you get going? How quick and obvious would that route feel to you? Report any hesitation, detour, need for help or reason to stop; if there is none, say so. Do not invent app behaviour or claim you executed anything.

Give a rating from 1.0 to 5.0 stars, in steps of 0.1. Keep these anchors: 1.0=cannot get going; 2.0=need substantial help; 3.0=can get going with detours; 4.0=clear with minor hesitation; 5.0=snappy and obvious throughout. Use values between anchors when they fit your experience better. Rate the route to the first visible result (the game), not full Prework completion or course quality. Report predicted getting going separately from smoothness.

Quote the instruction most relevant to your rating. Name the one change that would help you most, if any; none is allowed. Under 250 words. Return JSON with stars (number from 1.0 to 5.0 in steps of 0.1), wouldGetGoing (yes, no, or uncertain), firstActions (array), hesitations (array; empty if none), evidenceQuote (exact instruction text), feeling (your own voice), biggestImprovement (text; none if no change needed).

Where the HTML says to assume a video is here, assume the described demonstration is available. Do not invent content beyond its caption.

hesitations: The 'Make my first game' button sits under a paragraph about folders, so I might briefly wonder whether I should be reading more first.
Step 1 has four sub-steps, and the Mac-only folder step and 'if you see a choice between modes' are small points where I might pause.
The Mac/Windows toggle is not obviously needed; I might ignore it, which is fine on Mac.
The video is only a placeholder description, so if it were absent I'd rely on text alone, which still seems enough.

The Prework page is long below the game steps (download, calendar), but I could stop after step 3 and still have the payoff.
judgements.evidenceQuote: When Claude says it saved the game, open `Documents → agents-101 → prework` and double-click `snake.html` to play.
judgements.feeling: I think I'd actually get there. The welcome promises a playable game, and one button drops me straight into the steps. The only wobble is not knowing exactly what the mode choice looks like.
judgements.biggestImprovement: Add a one-line expectation after the Send step, such as 'Claude will take a minute or two; you'll see it say the game is saved', so I know what to wait for before looking for the file.

hesitations: The Start page says to make a folder, and the real steps are on a separate Prework section below. The link jumps there, so this is a small hop.
Step 1 has several nested clicks (Project or folder, Add folder, Documents, New Folder, Create, Open). On a skim I might miss one, though the video placeholder helps.
'If you see a choice between modes' is vague. I would not be sure whether I had picked the right mode if no choice appears.
Step 2 tells me to look for agents-101 below the message box. If it is not visible, I am not told what to do.
Playing needs leaving Claude to find the file in Finder. The instruction is clear, but it is a handoff out of the app.

judgements.evidenceQuote: See `agents-101` below the message box? Click Copy below, paste into that box, and click Send.
judgements.feeling: I like that the game comes before any downloads, and the big 'Make my first game' button tells me where to start. The folder setup is a bit fiddly, but I'd keep going because the payoff is close. I'd only stop if Cowork didn't show up or the folder didn't appear below the box.

firstActions: Read the welcome: see the Snake preview and the 'Make a Snake game you can play' promise
Click the 'Make my first game' button, which jumps to step 1 in Prework
Open Claude Desktop, click New, choose Cowork if offered
Click Project or folder, then Add folder
On Mac: Documents, New Folder, name it agents-101, Create, Open
Allow the permission dialog if it names agents-101
Click Copy on the snake prompt, paste it into the message box, Send
When Claude says it saved the game, open Documents, agents-101, prework and double-click snake.html to play
hesitations: The Welcome says 'Try it in your browser', but the game only exists after the folder and prompt steps, so the three-step route is slightly less instant than the preview suggests.
Step 1 says 'If you see a choice between modes' without saying what that looks like, and 'Project or folder' may be easy to miss.
Step 1's Mac folder instruction is nested in a long sentence, and there's no visible Windows alternative unless I switch the toggle.
The 'Choose a tool' picker in the cover is closed and unexplained, so I'd wonder whether I needed it. I'd probably skip it because the Start link leads straight on.
I'd have to find the file in Finder myself. There's a fallback if it opens in an editor, which helps, but this is the step most likely to cause a stall.
The prompt asks for 'prework/snake.html' but doesn't say the prework folder will be created automatically, which could cause a brief doubt.
judgements.evidenceQuote: See `agents-101` below the message box? Click Copy below, paste into that box, and click Send.
judgements.feeling: The 'Make my first game' button reassured me, and the path is short: folder, copy-paste, double-click. I'd probably get there in a few minutes. I'd slow down at the folder dialog and again when hunting for snake.html in Finder. Nothing made me want to quit, but I'd feel the distance between the promise and the payoff.
judgements.biggestImprovement: After Claude saves the game, add a one-line prompt asking Claude to open it in the browser for me, so I don't have to navigate Finder to see the first result.
